source_acquisition.search_note: The inventory row was no_public_source_found and the local visual_sources directory was empty. The PDF p.1 link and exact README title verify the official repository. Its tree has five matching exported assets (teaser, framework, main_results, individual_dataset_results, qualitative_comparison) but no plot/table source files; the remaining PDF objects have no public visual source. All repository inspection used read-only gh commands.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Figures use categorical red/blue/green/orange method coding plus grayscale masks and colored callouts; tables use black PDF text with pale red proposed rows, pale blue comparison cells, and blue citation text.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: Captions, table text, rules, and some PDF text are vector PDF objects; Figures 1–8 are dominated by embedded raster assets/plots. No editable plotting source was found in the official repository.
paper_style.style_consistency: Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern typography and directional metric headers are consistent across tables. Figure palettes vary by task and rely heavily on hue; method labels and line styles provide only partial redundancy.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. Motivation and efficiency overview. (a) Illustration of challenges including sample imbalance and complexity. (b) Quantitative results showing clear improvements using only 30% of the data. (c) Qualitative results validating our robustness in complex scenes.

color.semantic_mapping: Histogram colors encode target/background complexity; radial sectors encode detector and method; cyan/red/yellow marks and text identify local qualitative comparisons.

encodings.x: target/background complexity or detector radial sector
encodings.text: method names, values, and Missed Target

figures.data_and_statistics: Panel (a) sketches target/background complexity distributions without bin definitions or total sample counts; (b) shows labelled 30%-training-data results across detectors; (c) shows representative input/zoom/mask cases. No seeds, intervals, aggregation rule, or denominator is shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Introduction sample-imbalance and 30% practical claims lead to Figure 1, then to Tables 1–2 and Figure 6. The qualitative cases are extended by Figures 3, 4, and 8; the figure is motivation rather than a population error estimate.
design_strengths: The three panels combine the problem distribution, a quantitative teaser, and a concrete failure case.
The fixed mask columns and direct method labels remain legible after reduction.
The public teaser asset makes the visual provenance traceable.
design_weaknesses: Distribution bins, sample denominator, and uncertainty are absent.
Conceptual, quantitative, and representative-case evidence share one panel group and require prose to separate their strength.
Multiple hues carry method semantics with weak grayscale redundancy.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a page-width sequence of distribution motivation, low-data result, and qualitative failure to frame one problem; pair it with a numeric table giving denominator and repetitions.

figures.label: Figure 2

caption.text: Figure 2. Overview of the proposed framework. (a) Bi-level dual-update framework performs joint sample rebalancing and label refinement. (b) Dynamic sample rebalancing is designed to weight training data. (c) Physics-induced diffusion annotation generates reliable pseudo-masks from single-point supervision in a learnable manner.

color.semantic_mapping: Panel fills distinguish sample, label, weighting, network, and diffusion modules; arrows and boxes encode feedback and computation rather than numeric values.

encodings.facet: (a) total framework, (b) sample branch, (c) annotation branch
encodings.text: module titles, detector names, α, Dθ, ρ, and u^(k)

figures.data_and_statistics: No numeric observations are plotted. Arrows encode upper-level feedback, lower-level detector optimization, heat-field iteration, and label aggregation; boxes encode computational boundaries. The word reliable describes the proposed mechanism and requires Tables 3–5/Figure 8 for empirical support.
figures.evidence_relation: Equations (1)–(4) and the three update paths in §3.1–§3.3 are compressed into the method interface; Figure 2 leads to Table 3 component ablations and Tables 4–5 annotation quality/time.
design_strengths: The top-level loop and its two most important branches are visible in one object.
Arrow direction and module titles expose the relation between α, θ, ω, detector response, and pseudo-mask.
The public framework asset matches the PDF content.
design_weaknesses: K, τ, ρ, β, superpixel implementation, and update schedules are not encoded.
Small equations and many arrows lose readability in the two-column reduction.
Module colors lack shape or line-style redundancy.
figures.reusable_pattern: Split a feedback-loop overview into total, sample, and label panels, preserving input–transform–output order while stating implementation parameters outside the drawing.

figures.label: Figure 3

caption.text: Figure 3. Qualitative comparison on the SIRST3 dataset. Columns from left to right: 3D surfaces of inputs, input images with labels and local magnification, Ours, LESPS, MCLC, and PAL predictions (the blue part on ALCLNet, the green part on DNANet).

color.semantic_mapping: Black/white masks encode foreground; blue and green bottom bands identify ALCLNet and DNANet blocks; cyan/green dashed ellipses and arrows mark missed targets.

encodings.facet: blue ALCLNet vs green DNANet blocks
encodings.text: method names, Label, Zoomed, Missed Target, All Missed

figures.data_and_statistics: Four representative SIRST3 scenes are shown as 3D input surfaces, input images with Label/Zoomed insets, and binary prediction masks. There are no sample counts, error totals, seeds, intervals, or aggregation; missed/all-missed annotations are case-level marks.
figures.evidence_relation: The SIRST3 detector-level result discussion in §4.2 points to Figure 3, while Table 1 supplies IoU/nIoU/Pd/Fa. Figures 4 and 8 extend the qualitative comparison to individual scenes and pseudo-mask methods.
design_strengths: A fixed row scene and column method order makes mask differences directly comparable.
The 3D surface and zoomed image expose low-SNR, merging, and boundary cases.
Detector color bands and public qualitative asset preserve provenance.
design_weaknesses: Many narrow columns make individual masks small.
Case selection and total failure rate are unspecified.
The z-axis meaning and detector color distinction are not fully described in the caption.
figures.reusable_pattern: Fix the qualitative grid to input/ground truth/method/error annotation, and add case-sampling and full-set error counts so representative panels do not stand in for aggregate evidence.

figures.label: Figure 4

caption.text: Figure 4. Qualitative comparison on three representative scenes. These results are obtained by ALCLNet.

color.semantic_mapping: Grayscale input/masks carry the main image semantics; blue bottom labels identify methods, and cyan/yellow/red boxes and annotations identify zooms and missed regions.

encodings.text: Input, Label, Zoomed, Ours, LESPS, MCLC, PAL

figures.data_and_statistics: Three representative scenes are compared under ALCLNet. The rows cover high-clutter, multi-target, and low-contrast examples as described by nearby prose; no complete-case count, sampling rule, false-alarm count, or uncertainty is provided.
figures.evidence_relation: The individual-dataset stability/robustness claim in §4.2 is illustrated by Figure 4 and quantified in Table 2. It is qualitative evidence, not a whole-dataset robustness estimate.
design_strengths: Fixed five-column order keeps Input/Label and four method masks aligned.
Zoomed insets make target footprint and separation visible in a narrow column.
The detector condition is stated in the caption.
design_weaknesses: The caption does not identify the scene type represented by each row.
No numerical metric or full failure count is bound to the examples.
Small black-background masks and color-only labels lose detail after reduction.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use a fixed Input–Label–Ours–baseline qualitative row under one detector, and state the scene-selection rule and quantitative failure boundary.

figures.label: Figure 5

caption.text: Figure 5. Analysis of the learned sample weight α. The left plot shows the correlation of α with target size (small to large diameter) and target shape (near-circular to irregular), while the right plot shows the distribution of target shape, target size and α.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue density points/colorbar encode sample density; red trend and orange/blue density curves encode α and target-variable distributions.

encodings.x: normalized target size or target shape
encodings.facet: Target Size vs Target Shape rows
encodings.text: α, Target Size, Target Shape, and Distribution labels

figures.data_and_statistics: The left panels show density-colored scatter points with a red smooth trend for target size/shape versus α; the right panels show filled density curves for target variables and α. The text states that α was aggregated over 100 runs, but no aggregation formula, correlation coefficient, interval, or smoothing rule is given.
figures.evidence_relation: The meta-classifier/sample-weight branch leads to Figure 5, then to Figure 6 selection efficiency, Figure 7 stability, and Table 3 B2 (α≡1). This is a mechanism diagnostic, not a tested correlation estimate.
design_strengths: Scatter and marginal distributions give complementary views of the learned weight.
Target Size and Target Shape are separated into row-level facets.
The density colorbar makes concentration visible.
design_weaknesses: No correlation statistic or uncertainty accompanies the trend.
Density normalization and sample denominator are unspecified.
The mixed palette is difficult to distinguish in grayscale.
figures.reusable_pattern: Pair a relationship plot with marginal distributions for a learned weight, but publish the density, smoothing, aggregation, and uncertainty definitions.

figures.label: Figure 6

caption.text: Figure 6. Data-efficiency on SIRST3 dataset across diverse networks, comparing Ours, LESPS, PAL, and MCLC under single-point supervision. Others are trained with full training datasets.

color.semantic_mapping: Ours/LESPS/PAL/MCLC map to red/blue/green/orange lines; gray is the plot grid.

figures.data_and_statistics: Four detector panels plot IoU at 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50% usage. Ours is the red solid curve with point labels; LESPS, PAL, and MCLC are shown as nearly horizontal full-data baselines. The prose states top 30% α-ranked selection can surpass full-data baselines, but no error bars, complete numeric table, or selection denominator is given.
figures.evidence_relation: Figure 5 α ranking leads to Figure 6 data selection and the Abstract 30% claim. The four architectures provide repetition across networks, but not seed-level uncertainty or broader datasets.
design_strengths: Shared usage and IoU axes make architecture-specific efficiency curves easy to scan.
Four network panels test whether the pattern is architecture-specific.
Point labels expose the approximate Ours trajectory.
design_weaknesses: Partial-data Ours and full-data baselines have different x-axis conditions.
The exact 30% point, repeated runs, and uncertainty are absent.
Thin colored lines become crowded in a single-column rendering.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use aligned small multiples for data-budget curves, but explicitly separate full-data baselines and provide point-level repetitions and exact values.

figures.label: Figure 7

caption.text: Figure 7. Convergence of sample-selection strategy and stability validation on SIRST3 under diverse seeds.

color.semantic_mapping: Learnable/Ours, Prior/PAL, Random/MCLC, and LESPS map to pink/green/blue/purple curves; gray is grid.

figures.data_and_statistics: Panel (a) compares learnable, prior-based, and random selection over epochs; panel (b) compares Ours, PAL, MCLC, and LESPS over five seeds. The prose claims smaller variance for Ours, but the figure gives no per-seed table, variance, interval, or aggregation rule; panel (a) data budget is also supplied only by prose.
figures.evidence_relation: The learned α ranking is tested first as a selection strategy and then as a stability claim. Table 3 B2/B4 gives related optimization controls, while Figure 6 supplies the data-efficiency consequence.
design_strengths: Convergence and seed validation are separated into two readable panels.
The seed points make between-run spread visible without hiding the categorical x condition.
Legends stay inside the panel boundaries.
design_weaknesses: Five connected seed points do not establish a variance estimate without summary statistics.
Caption omits the five-seed count, data budget, and comparator conditions.
Both panels share a visual style although their x-axis semantics differ.
figures.reusable_pattern: Place selection learning and seed-level stability side by side, while publishing seed values, summary intervals, and the fixed data budget.

figures.label: Figure 8

caption.text: Figure 8. Qualitative comparison of small target detection on the SIRST3 dataset: Ours vs. COM, MCLC, SAM, and SAM2.

color.semantic_mapping: Black/white mask and grayscale input carry the main encoding; red zoom boxes identify target locations and gray bottom bands identify columns.

encodings.text: Input, Label, Ours, COM, MCLC, SAM, SAM2

figures.data_and_statistics: Six representative SIRST3 scenes are shown as two three-row blocks: Ours/COM/MCLC and Ours/SAM/SAM2. The object has no sample count, selection rule, error count, threshold, prompt condition, or uncertainty; under-segmentation, over-growth, and missed-target readings are case-level observations.
figures.evidence_relation: Tables 4–5 provide pseudo-mask IoU/time; Figure 8 supplies the shape-level diagnostic for COM, MCLC, SAM, and SAM2. It closes the annotation-quality argument but cannot replace a full error audit.
design_strengths: Two baseline families are split into isomorphic blocks.
Input, zoom, label, and mask columns preserve the target footprint comparison.
Black-background/white-mask contrast is relatively grayscale-safe.
design_weaknesses: Representative scenes are not a whole-set error rate.
The row correspondence between upper and lower blocks is not explained in the caption.
Prompt, threshold, and mask-confidence conditions are absent.
figures.reusable_pattern: Use matched qualitative blocks for distinct baseline families and keep Input→Label→Ours→baseline ordering; accompany them with sampling, threshold, and error-count metadata.

tables.label: Table 1

caption.text: Table 1. Performance of ISTD under different training strategies. All models are trained on SIRST3 and evaluated on SIRST3 and three individual datasets (SIRST-v1, NUDT-SIRST, IRSTD-1k). We report four metrics: IoU (%), nIoU (%), Pd (%), and Fa (10−6).

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty display: every cell is a point estimate; no SD/SE, interval, seed aggregation, or hypothesis test is supplied.
tables.data_and_statistics: Seven detector row groups (MLCLNet, ALCLNet, DNANet, ISNet, UIUNet, GGLNet, MSDANet) are evaluated with Full, LESPS, PAL, MCLC, and Ours across SIRST3, SIRST-v1, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1k. Each dataset group contains IoU, nIoU, Pd, and Fa; two decimals are used throughout. Full is a fully supervised upper bound, while Ours is the proposed single-point strategy.
tables.evidence_relation: This is the main quantitative benchmark following Figure 1 motivation and Figure 2 framework; Figure 3 gives detector-level qualitative examples. The paper claims broad superiority among non-Full strategies, but individual Pd/Fa cells are not always best and no significance evidence is shown.
design_strengths: Dataset→metric hierarchy and detector groups allow broad cross-condition scanning.
Metric arrows and units make higher/lower directions explicit.
浅红/浅蓝 cell fill gives a quick proposed/best-cell cue.
design_weaknesses: Thirty-five rows and eighteen columns make values small at page scale.
The highlighter rule is not defined in the caption.
No repetitions, denominators, seed summaries, or uncertainty accompany strong textual claims.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use dataset top-level groups, metric-direction headers, and detector row groups for a main benchmark; add a declared highlight rule and repeated-run uncertainty.

tables.label: Table 2

caption.text: Table 2. Performance of ISTD under different training strategies. Models are trained on three individual datasets (SIRST-v1, NUDT-SIRST, IRSTD-1k). We report four metrics: IoU (%), nIoU (%), Pd (%), and Fa (10−6).

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty display: table entries are point estimates only and omit repetitions, intervals, and significance tests.
tables.data_and_statistics: ALCLNet, DNANet, UIUNet, and MSDANet are each trained on SIRST-v1, NUDT-SIRST, and IRSTD-1k. The five strategies are Full, LESPS, PAL, MCLC, and Ours; each dataset group reports IoU, nIoU, Pd, and Fa to two decimals.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 2 controls the training-dataset condition left implicit in Table 1 and supports the individual-dataset robustness prose; Figure 4 supplies ALCLNet qualitative scenes. The claimed consistent/significant gain is not paired with seed or test statistics.
design_strengths: The dataset condition becomes an explicit top-level header rather than a prose footnote.
The same metric order and color convention as Table 1 makes comparisons reusable.
Four architectures repeat the individual-dataset test.
design_weaknesses: The fourteen-column table remains dense in the two-column page.
Caption omits split and seed conditions.
Highlight and missing statistical rules are not defined.
tables.reusable_pattern: Separate cross-dataset training controls into a wide table with stable metric headers and explicit condition labels.

tables.label: Table 3

caption.text: Table 3. Ablation of core components in our framework. These results are obtained by ALCLNet.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty display: one ALCLNet/SIRST3 point estimate is reported for each variant.
tables.data_and_statistics: Rows A1–A4 isolate naive point supervision, diffusion, superpixel prior, and their numerical combination; rows B1–B4 remove direct joint learning alternatives, α balance, online label update, and dynamic aggregation; Proposed is the complete method. Columns are SIRST3 IoU, nIoU, and Pd with a two-level SIRST3/metric header.
tables.evidence_relation: Figure 2 defines the two branches; Table 3 separates supervision quality (A block) from optimization path (B block), then Figures 5–7 diagnose α and selection. A1 IoU 8.07 is an explicit failure control; B1/B4 test simple no-feedback alternatives.
design_strengths: A/B row labels keep pseudo-label and optimization mechanisms distinct.
Naive failure and full Proposed rows bound the mechanism comparison.
ALCLNet condition is stated in the caption.
design_weaknesses: Fa is omitted even though it is a main ISTD metric elsewhere.
There is no factorial combination, cross-architecture repetition, or uncertainty.
The inset grid is small and `numerical`/β semantics require prose.
tables.reusable_pattern: Group ablations by mechanism family and retain a naive failure plus complete row; report all headline metrics and repeated conditions.

tables.label: Table 4

caption.text: Table 4. Pseudo-mask generation on four ISTD datasets with Centroid and Coarse initialization, comparing COM, MCLC, and Ours, and reporting IoU and average time per target.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty display: IoU and average time are point summaries with no repeated-run spread or hardware variation.
tables.data_and_statistics: Centroid and Coarse initialization are two row groups. Each contains COM, MCLC, and Ours; columns are SIRST3, SIRST-v1, NUDT-SIRST, IRSTD-1k IoU (two decimals) and Average Time (seconds, three decimals). Centroid Ours is 68.02/74.58/64.48/70.12 and 0.012s; Coarse Ours is 65.69/73.78/59.15/68.42 and 0.013s.
tables.evidence_relation: Equations (2)–(4) motivate physics diffusion/superpixel; Table 4 binds that mechanism to pseudo-mask quality and CPU per-target cost, then Figure 8 gives mask-shape cases. The speed comparison is annotation-only, not end-to-end training cost.
design_strengths: Quality and time share one initialization grouping.
Centroid/Coarse sensitivity is visible without changing table structure.
Time units and IoU direction are in the header.
design_weaknesses: CPU model, timing protocol, and aggregation are absent.
Cell-fill rule is not described in the caption.
No uncertainty or significance accompanies initialization differences.
tables.reusable_pattern: Place pseudo-label quality and annotation cost beside each other under each initialization, with hardware and timing protocol stated.

tables.label: Table 5

caption.text: Table 5. Pseudo-mask generation on four ISTD datasets with Centroid and Coarse initialization, comparing SAM, SAM2, and Ours, reporting IoU and average time per target.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty display: all IoU/time entries are point summaries without repeated runs, intervals, or hardware variation.
tables.data_and_statistics: Centroid and Coarse groups each compare SAM, SAM2, and Ours on four dataset IoUs plus average seconds per target. Centroid Ours is 68.02/74.58/64.48/70.12 at 0.012s; Coarse Ours is 65.69/73.78/59.15/68.42 at 0.013s. IoU uses two decimals and time uses three decimals plus s.
tables.evidence_relation: Table 5 extends Table 4 from COM/MCLC to foundation-model baselines and supplies the upper/lower blocks of Figure 8. It supports dedicated physics annotation under two initialization conditions, but prompt, model version, and compute boundary are not fully specified.
design_strengths: The table is structurally isomorphic to Table 4, enabling baseline-family comparison.
The very low Coarse SAM scores make input-condition sensitivity explicit.
Quality and per-target time remain on one decision surface.
design_weaknesses: SAM/SAM2 prompt and inference versions are not described in the caption.
Compute boundaries may not be equivalent across methods.
No uncertainty, significance, or failure counts are reported.
tables.reusable_pattern: Keep generic foundation baselines and dedicated methods in the same initialization/cost table while fixing prompt, version, hardware, and timing semantics.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 frames imbalance, low-data efficiency, and qualitative failure; Figure 2 defines the dual-update/diffusion loop; Tables 1–2 establish detector and dataset comparisons; Figures 3–5 supply qualitative and α mechanism evidence; Table 3 separates supervision and optimization ablations; Figures 6–7 test selection efficiency and stability; Tables 4–5 combine pseudo-mask quality with annotation time; Figure 8 closes with mask-level baseline failures.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use Figure/Table numbering followed by a short title. Figure 1–2 enumerate panel duties; Figure 1, 2 use stronger wording about improvements/reliable pseudo-masks, while Figures 3–8 and Tables 1–5 mostly state setup and comparison without interval or seed definitions. Most captions are not independently bold headline sentences.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Tables 1–2 use dataset as the top header and IoU/nIoU/Pd/Fa as the second level; Table 3 uses SIRST3 then metrics; Tables 4–5 use initialization/dataset/time then IoU/time. Direction arrows and two-level metric headers are stable, while pale cell fills carry proposed/best cues without caption definitions.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 2’s α/θ/ω feedback interface feeds Tables 1–2; Figure 3–4 qualitative effects and Table 3 A/B blocks test the mechanism; Figure 5 links α to selection; Figures 6–7 test data efficiency/stability; Tables 4–5 and Figure 8 test pseudo-mask quality and cost.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: There is no appendix or supplementary material. All 8 figures and 5 tables are main-text objects on p.2–8; implementation parameters, extra failures, seed aggregation, and statistical tests are absent rather than moved to an appendix.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: PDF table/caption text uses Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern math objects at roughly 6–7 pt in tables and 9–10 pt in captions; raster figure internals use heterogeneous serif/sans-serif estimates and cannot be recovered as source settings.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Pale red proposed rows and pale blue comparison cells recur in tables, while figures use red/blue/green/orange method curves and grayscale mask backgrounds. Hue is often the primary method encoding, so grayscale robustness is weaker for Figures 1 and 3–7 than for the tables and Figure 8.

most_reusable_patterns: Figure 2’s three-level feedback diagram makes sample weighting, pseudo-label generation, and detector response one visible interface.
Tables 1–2 use stable dataset→metric headers and architecture row groups for broad comparisons.
Table 3 separates pseudo-label and optimization mechanisms with A/B blocks and a complete Proposed row.
Tables 4–5 place pseudo-mask IoU and per-target time under matched initialization groups.
Figures 6–7 use small multiples to separate data-budget and seed-stability questions.
highest_value_objects: Figure 2 for the method interface and feedback direction.
Table 1 for the cross-detector/four-dataset headline comparison.
Table 3 for compact mechanism decomposition including the naive failure.
Tables 4–5 for the quality–annotation-time decision surface.
Figure 5 for the learned α mechanism diagnostic.
failure_patterns: Point-estimate tables and curves omit repeated-run spread, intervals, and significance tests.
Figure 1 mixes conceptual distributions, a quantitative teaser, and representative cases without denominators.
Figures 3, 4, and 8 show selected cases without selection rules or whole-set error rates.
Figure 6 puts partial-data Ours and full-data baselines on one usage axis, inviting condition confusion.
Figure 7 uses five connected seeds to support a variance claim without reporting variance.
Tables 4–5 omit complete CPU/prompt/version/hardware semantics, and no appendix supplies the missing details.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper visualizes the point-supervised ISTD bottleneck with a motivation triptych and a feedback-loop framework, then uses cross-detector/dataset tables for point-estimate gains and qualitative, α, data-budget, seed, and cost objects to expose mechanism and boundary conditions.
